prompts.street:
Japanese TV anime style key frame, like a frame from a slice-of-life anime series (not a painting, not photorealistic, not 3D): clean confident line art, flat cel shading with crisp two-tone shadows, bright saturated summer colours, backgrounds drawn in the same clean anime style. Warm golden sunlight, cool lavender shadows, luminous blue summer sky and big cumulus clouds.
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: architectural art-direction concept for Harumachi: Next Summer, a Japanese mountain-foot life simulation.
Primary request: a convincing intimate Japanese neighborhood shopping street with FOUR individually designed, richly detailed small shops. They must have radically different silhouettes, floor heights, roof shapes, window rhythm, frontage depth and occupation, while belonging to one beautiful summer anime world. Architecture must feel lived in for decades, human scale, rich near-view clarity and charming owner-specific life. This is a new proposed redesign, not a screenshot edit. Attached game screenshot is only context for the town and genre: replace the repetitive white timber box aesthetic.
Composition: wide landscape horizontal illustration, pedestrian eye height with a slight three-quarter perspective down the street. All four shop fronts clearly visible, very little empty foreground. Focus on architectural design and readable medium details; no UI and no characters blocking buildings.
LEFT TO RIGHT:
1. Wakako's old grocery: a squat Showa-era corner shop, olive-green painted timber and cream plaster, low staggered roof, faded mint retractable striped awning with one visibly patched panel, deep open entrance and produce display in front. Separate real-shaped cabbages, carrots, cucumbers and tomatoes in wood/plastic crates, weighing scale, enamel milk sign with a simple bottle icon, stock door, stacked delivery boxes, baskets, roll-down shutter housing, small upper sliding window with bamboo blind. There is a clear walking gap through its frontage. Slight wear at handles and lower wall only.
2. Ren's renovated neighborhood bakery: narrower and taller building, warm ivory plaster with reddish brick at its base, offset projecting bay display window, a small distinct front gable, warm yellow awning, projecting wooden loaf-shaped sign, visible oven chimney on one side. Baskets of individually shaped breads, half-height curtain, tidy flower pot, flour delivery crates by a side hatch and a little outdoor bench. This shop is young and well cared for, not rustic fantasy.
3. Chiyo's florist: low asymmetric shop with a glass-and-timber lean-to greenhouse annex and a higher roof behind it. Transparent patterned glazing frames, slender pergola, vine around a downpipe, suspended baskets, tiered flower stands, hydrangeas and bouquets, water tap, galvanized watering can, hose neatly coiled, damp moss ONLY close to the tap. Floral density and depth, an obvious recessed entrance.
4. Aken's zakka: a dark-brown timber machiya storefront with low horizontal tiled eaves, genuine fine vertical lattice, recessed sliding entry, indigo noren, an understated warm porch lantern, a small vertical side sign decorated with a simple bowl icon. Umbrella stand, pottery shelf, bamboo baskets, two wind chimes, a side alley leading to a small storage annex. Separate upper narrow plaster vent windows, distinctly older than the bakery.
Street life: subtle overhead service wires and wall brackets, gutter transitions, varied drain covers and paving edges, a parked delivery bicycle at the grocery, localized plants, faded layers where a former sign was removed. Shops slightly vary in frontage setback, spacing and roof height. Keep plain wall areas and pauses between clusters for visual hierarchy. Open street remains navigable. No torii, no shrine decoration on ordinary shops, no cyberpunk or neon, no giant lantern chains, no luxury shopping street. Clean rectilinear frames, straight structural beams, correct consistent perspective, believable Japanese scale. Nothing looks melted, warped, repetitive, or generated from one kit. No fine photographic texture, grain or noisy clutter. No unreadable pseudo-lettering; signs use simple recognizable pictorial emblems.
prompts.homes:
Japanese TV anime style key frame, like a frame from a slice-of-life anime series (not a painting, not photorealistic, not 3D): clean confident line art, flat cel shading with crisp two-tone shadows, bright saturated summer colours, backgrounds drawn in the same clean anime style. Warm golden sunlight, cool lavender shadows, luminous blue summer sky and big cumulus clouds.
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: detailed residential architecture concept sheet for Harumachi: Next Summer.
Primary request: show TWO very distinct Japanese homes with exceptional lived-in detail, intelligible architecture, believable construction and clear close-up quality. The supplied current game image is a context reference only; redesign its generic box houses so they have individuality and strong Japanese residential character.
Composition: a wide landscape diptych, two equally sized architectural three-quarter views side by side, quietly separated by a slim ivory gutter. Each view shows a full building, its front AND one side, grounds, roof and meaningful house details. No labels or written captions. Human scale, no dollhouse exaggeration, no characters needed. Minimal unused sky/foreground. Readable silhouette first, larger architectural details second, small clustered props last.
LEFT: the grandmother's old family home. A modest compact L-shaped Japanese timber house with a two-storey rear portion and a long lower engawa wing, not a square symmetrical villa. Slightly offset slate-blue/charcoal tiled roof masses, deep eaves, clear rafter ends and ridge cap detail, old dark cedar lower cladding and soft ivory upper plaster. Upper windows are asymmetric and smaller, with storm shutters and a half-lowered bamboo blind. The low wing has wooden sliding glass/shoji doors and a raised timber veranda, two or three stepping stones leading through a tiny garden. Thoughtful rain chain draining into a ceramic basin, hydrangea by the shaded wall, aged ceramic plant pots, a small vegetable-growing box, cloth laundry towel on a discreet line, old bamboo broom at the side service door, intercom and house plate, a repaired replacement wooden board in a slightly fresher colour. A grandfather-style stool and summer mosquito coil holder on the engawa, cat sleeping spot in shade. Garden wall is low and partly interrupted with a modest timber gate; a few irregular trees and clipped shrubs frame the home rather than hiding it. A plausible rear kitchen lean-to and visible service gutter connect the main masses.
RIGHT: a small Showa wooden apartment building, a long narrow two-storey structure with three upper units and three lower units. Low charcoal tile roof with a small corrugated-metal service awning, muted warm pale-ochre plaster and dark timber panels. External galvanised STEEL staircase on the far side and a continuous narrow upper balcony with clean thin steel rails, not generic chunky wooden rails. Upper doors recessed into shade. Each unit is clearly lived in by a different person: one with neatly arranged plants and a blue towel; one with a pale laundry sheet and a bicycle helmet by its doorway; one with lowered reed blind and no plants. Downstairs a row of varied slightly worn mailboxes, six modest utility meters and conduits, separate wall-mounted AC compressors, one delivery bicycle and one older bicycle, umbrella rack and a small shoe rack. Little side alley, patch of weeds at the drain, patched downspout, one newer cream window frame contrasted with older timber ones. Curtains and door colours vary subtly, no modern luxury apartment appearance, no excessive colourful chaos.
Constraints: two totally different building silhouettes, distinct age and household story, strong Japanese everyday detail. Do NOT repeat the previous generic identical blue gable + white plaster + large framed windows style. Straight, crisp posts, rails, door grids and frames; consistent architectural perspective. Solid functional construction; no warped AI edges. Colours feel sunny and hopeful. Weathering is sparse, hand-drawn and localized, not photorealistic dirt. No fantasy temple, no torii, no neon, no European shutters, no red lantern chains. No written text or UI.
